fact: The Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board said on 3 September 2025 that over 90 percent of Pennsylvania sports wagering is placed on online platforms, and that the Board itself takes bettor complaints and disputes against licensed operators and investigates them, a service it cannot offer if the problem is with an offshore site.

Pennsylvania runs self-exclusion as four separate Board lists (casinos and offsite venues such as off-track betting, interactive gambling, video gaming terminals, and fantasy contests); casino bans of one or five years stay in force until you ask to come off, the others lapse when the chosen term ends, and breaking an exclusion means winnings are confiscated. The Board's page does not name a sports-wagering list, but its September 2025 release says the self-exclusion programme blocks access to all Board-regulated online betting sites.

The Pennsylvania Act (4 Pa.C.S. Chapter 13C, added 30 October 2017 as Act 42) defines a sporting event as a professional or collegiate sports or athletic event or a motor race event, and defines sports wagering to include bets on athletes' individual performance statistics.

Hollywood Casino at Penn National Race Course took Pennsylvania's first legal sports bet on 15 November 2018, a $20 wager on the Steelers to win the Super Bowl (secondary: The Philadelphia Inquirer, 3 December 2018).
West Virginia's first legal sports bet was taken on 30 August 2018 at Hollywood Casino at Charles Town Races (secondary: WCHS-TV, 30 August 2018).
State law allows at most five sports wagering licences, available only to the state's racetrack and historic resort casinos, and every sports wager is a West Virginia Lottery game owned by the state.
Each West Virginia licence holder may run no more than three individually branded online sportsbook sites and apps (rule 179-9-12.1).

West Virginia's Sports Wagering Act defines sports events to include any collegiate sport or athletic event and defines sports wagering to include bets on athletes' individual performance statistics; it also excludes daily fantasy sports.

The Racing and Gaming Commission's sports wagering regulations (K.A.R. 112-201 through 112-204), whose current text carries an effective date of 11 September 2026 after temporary rules effective 12 August 2022, ban sportsbooks from describing an advertisement or promotion as free of risk.

Kansas has its own Sports Wagering Exclusion Program, run by the Racing and Gaming Commission and separate from the casino Voluntary Exclusion Program: enrolling disables all active sports wagering accounts, blocks new ones and cannot be undone early, casino exclusion participants who joined after 1 September 2022 are barred from sports wagering too, and if you self-exclude with a bet still open it settles and any winnings or pushed stake go to the state problem gambling grant fund.

Kansas law (2022 Senate Bill 84) limits each of the four state-owned casinos to three sports wagering platforms, forbids any line of credit to a bettor, requires you to be physically in Kansas to bet online, and does not treat an event as a sporting event if most of its participants are under 18.

Kansas sportsbooks at the four state-owned casinos began taking in-person and mobile bets on 1 September 2022, with the official opening on 8 September (secondary: KWCH-TV, 18 August 2022, reporting Governor Laura Kelly's announcement).
North Carolina law does not authorise sports wagering on youth sports, or on injuries, penalties, the outcome of disciplinary proceedings, or the outcome of replay reviews.

A North Carolina online operator can only be licensed if it has a written designation agreement with a professional sports team, a motorsports facility, a facility hosting a yearly professional golf event, or a NASCAR or golf sanctioning body, and each of those partners may sign with only one operator.

The Commission's Voluntary Exclusion Program lets you pick one year, three years, five years or lifetime, covers sports and pari-mutuel wagering, does not reach tribal lands, and early removal needs a reinstatement session followed by a 30 day wait.

North Carolina's Commission rules bar operators from calling a promotion "free" unless it costs the player nothing, or free of risk if the player must lose or risk their own money to use it or withdraw winnings.

Vermont's law lets the state contract two to six mobile sportsbooks; the Department of Liquor and Lottery chose three (DraftKings, FanDuel and Fanatics Sportsbook) and mobile betting launched on 11 January 2024. There is no retail option.

Vermont bars wagers on any college game involving a college team based in Vermont unless it is part of a tournament, and bars any high school or college event played in Vermont; bets on athletes' individual performance statistics are part of the legal definition of sports wagering.

Vermont forbids funding a sports wagering account with a credit card (31 V.S.A. 1340(d)(2)) and allows one account per person per operator; the Board's procedures, adopted 13 May 2026 and dated 1 October 2026, also bar wagers on injuries or penalties, bar calling a promotion free of risk if you must risk your own money, and block betting once lifetime deposits pass $2,500, and again each year after, until you acknowledge it and can set limits or close the account.

Vermont's statewide self-exclusion list is run by the Department; you choose 1, 3 or 5 years or lifetime, a lifetime choice cannot be undone, and fantasy sports need a separate opt-in with each fantasy operator.
Wyoming taxes online sports wagering at 10 percent of the prior month's revenue, and the first $300,000 each fiscal year goes to county programmes that prevent and treat problem gambling.
Wyoming's minimum age for online sports wagering is 18, not 21 (W.S. 9-24-105; the helpline file already carries 18).

Wyoming's statute counts collegiate events as sporting events, its rules exclude only events where most athletes are under 18, and its rules ban wagers on the injury of a participant; I found no in-state college ban in the text read.

Wyoming's Gaming Commission voted unanimously on 22 November 2024 to put anyone found guilty of harassing an athlete on the state's involuntary exclusion list (rule text, Chapter 8 Section 3(a)(i); the vote date is from the trade outlet reprinted on the Commission's page, so secondary).

Maryland has barred player-specific proposition bets on college participants since 1 March 2024, a directive from the Lottery and Gaming agency to sportsbooks rather than a statute; a 2026 bill (HB 518) would have written it into law and its page shows no action past Senate second reading, so I found no sign it was enacted.

Maryland's sports wagering regulations bar bets on high school events, bar bets on any amateur event (college included) unless the Commission specifically approves it, bar wagers on injuries, penalties, player disciplinary rulings and replay reviews, and cap any one bettor's wager on one event at $5,000,000.
Sports winnings in Maryland that go unclaimed for 182 days after the wager is won revert to the state's Problem Gambling Fund.
Maryland's Voluntary Exclusion Program covers sports wagering in person and online, the minimum stay on the list is two years (or lifetime), and removal is never automatic.

Illinois bars every wager on a sports event involving an Illinois collegiate team, in person as well as online, because the in-person exception (tier 1 wagers not tied to an individual athlete) ran only until 1 July 2024; it also bars minor league events and kindergarten through 12th grade events. The CSV note says "No online wagers", which understates this.

Since 1 July 2025 Illinois has charged each online sportsbook a wager tax of $0.25 on each of its first 20,000,000 online wagers a year and $0.50 on each wager after that; it is levied on the operator, not the bettor, and a further 2 percent of adjusted gross receipts on wagers placed inside Cook County goes to the county's criminal justice system.

Illinois sports bettors who self-exclude use the Gaming Board's Self-Exclusion Program, which has covered sports wagering since the 2019 Sports Wagering Act, and enrolment must be done in person (about 30 to 45 minutes, photo ID required) at Gaming Board offices in the casinos or other sanctioned sites, including some in Iowa.

Colorado made it unlawful for an internet sportsbook to accept a credit card deposit, directly or through an account funded by a credit card, under Senate Bill 26-131 (signed 1 June 2026, effective date set by the act as 12 August 2026, with a maximum Commission penalty of $25,000); on 15 October 2026 the Division of Gaming's Bulletin 17 told operators to decline any prepaid card deposit whose funding source they cannot verify was not a credit card.
The same Colorado act caps an internet sportsbook at six separate deposits per person per gaming day and bars it from sending push notifications or texts that solicit bets or deposits.
Colorado voters approved Proposition DD, which legalised and taxed sports betting to fund state water projects, on 5 November 2019 by 800,745 yes votes to 756,712 no.
Colorado keeps one Exclusion List covering casinos and sportsbooks; a person on it may not participate or collect winnings and forfeits money wagered after being added.

New York limits credit card funding to $2,500 per year for each account with each operator, and once an account's lifetime deposits pass $2,500 the operator must block all betting until the bettor acknowledges it, after which the bettor can set limits or close the account.

New York's age is set by statute: a "minor" is anyone under 21 (fills the blank min_age), and mobile bets are legally accepted by equipment at a licensed commercial casino, with the Gaming Commission, not the operators, controlling which sports and leagues are on the menu.

In a letter to leagues dated 4 February 2026 the Gaming Commission said it is re-examining all game-specific individual player proposition wagers and single-game multi-leg individual player parlays and will prohibit some outright if its review requires it.

New York's Voluntary Self-Exclusion covers sports wagering along with all other New York gaming, lasts one year, three years, five years or lifetime, needs a form and photo handed in at a gaming facility, at Commission headquarters, or mailed notarised, and any winnings made while excluded are forfeited.

Connecticut allows only three online sports betting skins by statute (one each for the Mashantucket Pequot Tribe and the Mohegan Tribe, one for the Connecticut Lottery Corporation outside the reservations), and the Department of Consumer Protection's FAQ currently lists three platforms: DraftKings, FanDuel and Bet Fanatics.

Beyond the college rule already on the page, Connecticut teams can only be backed to win a tournament of four or more intercollegiate teams, the wager must cover all the tournament's games and be placed before it starts, and single games involving a Connecticut team are never allowed, even inside a tournament.
Connecticut allows credit cards for betting but limits a person to one debit card or one credit card per account and requires operators to put a monetary limit on credit card use.

Connecticut's self-exclusion list lets you choose one year, five years or lifetime, bars you from collecting winnings or recovering losses, and lets operators extend the ban to their offerings in other states.
